edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: older adults with polysomnography or EEG data
edges.mechanism: Low slow-wave sleep has a biologically plausible route to worse dementia (all-cause), and the mechanism is consistent with the kinds of tissues or systems most directly exposed.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Zhang meta analysis in Sleep Med Rev already points to low slow-wave sleep tracks with higher risk or worse outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
